races.name: Coral Kincsem Heritage Handicap

runners_data.name: Bourbon Blues
runners_data.note: Course specialist with four runs at Goodwood including a third over 1m2f here; genuine hold-up style suits a strongly-run race, and Good to Firm is confirmed fine, though his form string (2-3060) shows patchy recent consistency worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Bourbon Blues nonetheless catches the eye as the top-rated runner in a field of 14, and experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; third and second two and one runs back respectively suggest he retains ability, and 26 days between runs leaves him fresh.

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front runner, which is his natural position and a clear advantage in a field this congested with pace — however, his STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects that he has been racing away from this role, and his trainer's 14-day record (3/43) is modest.
runners_data.comment: Evanesco landed a win three starts back and returns in good order on 20 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour — the risk is that two modest efforts since that success, including a fifth last time out, must be overcome.

runners_data.name: Harmonics
runners_data.note: Won twice in four runs including over 1m at Goodwood for Gosden; stepping up to 1m2f looks a logical progression, and a 40-day break under Shane Foley for a sharp yard (7/19 T14) is not concerning on this evidence.
runners_data.comment: Harmonics has back-to-back wins two and three starts back to his name, but he managed only eighth last time out and arrives 40 days later needing to bounce back; he has run over today's trip before and draws stall three carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Gonna Fly
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won over 1m2f for Ralph Beckett and looks well-suited by the trip; Hector Crouch is a shrewd booking, though a soft-ground win in the form string raises a slight query on Good to Firm, mitigated by other quicker-ground placings.
runners_data.comment: Gonna Fly won two starts back but was fifth last time out, and his distance-and-going experience is a plus; 130 lb from stall eleven is no small ask, however, and he'll need to bounce back sharply to make his presence felt here.

runners_data.name: Savvy Disko
runners_data.note: Two wins from four runs including over 9f at Goodwood; Billy Loughnane is an in-form jockey and the horse clearly handles the track, though the trainer's T14 figure (0/9) suggests the yard is running cold right now.
runners_data.comment: Savvy Disko won his last two starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a 33-day absence and a stiff 129 lb from stall 12 are factors to weigh against that encouragingly consistent recent form.

runners_data.name: Decade Of Time
runners_data.note: Won over 1m at Goodwood and over 1m on soft, stepping up to 1m2f for the first time; Jack Channon is hitting form (4/19 T14) and Tom Marquand is a strong rider in big fields, making this an interesting projection run.
runners_data.comment: Decade Of Time landed back-to-back wins in his last four starts before a runner-up effort most recently, so the recent form reads well, but a ranking of tenth in this field and 129 lb to carry are significant asks.

runners_data.name: Birgham Dub
runners_data.note: Won over 1m2f on soft and placed at listed level, but his last three runs include a 10th and a 5th at this track over longer trips, suggesting form is patchy; 42 days off for Jane Chapple-Hyam and Oisin Murphy is a strong jockey booking that demands respect.
runners_data.comment: Showed his best with back-to-back wins in recent starts but has been unplaced last time out, and 42 days off adds a fitness query; has experience of today's going, though our rating of 98 suggests there's ability to tap into from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Lion of Alba
runners_data.note: Course winner over 1m who is in truth a prominent type forced into a midfield mapping by sheer numbers at the head of affairs — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) reflects the positional compromise, and his recent form (51-747) shows he has not built on that win.
runners_data.comment: Lion of Alba's win four starts back and his experience on today's going make him a legitimate threat here, and 21 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the risk is that he's been out of the first three in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Dial Me In
runners_data.note: Trained by Joseph O'Brien, whose yard is in sharp form (16/67 T14); a genuine pace-presser by nature but mapped to midfield here due to field congestion, and his last run was a well-beaten 13th at this track over 1m4f, which limits confidence.
runners_data.comment: Dial Me In shaped well when second two starts back and has previous experience over today's trip and going, while a trainer firing at 28% makes him a serious contender from stall 4; the worry is that last-time-out unplaced run leaves something to prove on current form.

runners_data.name: Dark Whisper
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three starts and clearly progressive, but all three runs have been over 1m and today's step to 1m2f is unproven; Jamie Spencer will get him settled, and he is a natural front-presser who will find the positional picture against him here.
runners_data.comment: Dark Whisper arrives here rated bottom two of 14 on our figures and ranked 13th overall, making him hard to fancy despite a win last time out; his experience on today's going is the one genuine foothold to cling to.

runners_data.name: Strength Of Spirit
runners_data.note: Six-race form string with two wins but pattern of fading (138934) suggests vulnerability in competitive fields; a natural prominent runner who won't hold his position today, and the trainer (K.R. Burke) is cold at 0/12 in the 14-day window.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back but has struggled for consistency, with a ninth and a fourth in between suggesting he blows hot and cold; has run over today's going before, carries 121 lb from stall 10, and a trainer firing at 34% offers encouragement.

runners_data.name: Ciarrai Abu
runners_data.note: Won twice at Goodwood over 1m but steps up sharply in trip and in class today; a prominent runner by style who will find many horses ahead of him in this race shape, and Harry Eustace's 14-day record (3/12) is acceptable without being compelling.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Ciarrai Abu is hard to fancy despite winning last time out and a second win three starts back; the fourth-placed effort two starts back and a sixth five starts back temper enthusiasm, and his speed rating of 78 leaves him well short of the top-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Loz Vegas
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a consistent but uninspiring recent form string (58-654); course experience is solid and Marco Ghiani is capable, but the trainer (Peter Chapple-Hyam) at 0/5 in 14 days and an OR of 85 make this an each-way proposition at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than fourth, Loz Vegas faces a stiff task from stall six off 120 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 92 hints at some unexploited ability.

runners_data.name: Lean d'Aislingean
runners_data.note: Lightly raced hold-up horse trained by Charlie Pike (0/9 T14) with only three runs, all over 1m; the step to 1m2f may actually suit given her staying-on placed efforts, but she remains unexposed and the trainer's cold form is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Lean d'Aislingean faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's going before and those placings on his last two starts show some ability, but the gulf to the top-rated runners looks significant from stall one.

races.paceDynamic: Evanesco is the confirmed front runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a 14-runner field, is well placed to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood's undulating 1m2f track. The field is, however, saturated with prominent-style horses — Lion of Alba, Dial Me In, Dark Whisper, Strength Of Spirit and Ciarrai Abu are all natural pace-pressing types who cannot all secure their preferred berth, meaning Evanesco may face some early pressure from rivals scrambling to settle near the front rather than the uncontested lead the pace map implies. The net effect is likely to be a race run at a fair but not brutal tempo, with a queue of horses racing slightly out of position behind a front runner who is in his natural role but may not be entirely unchallenged. This shape — a controlled but honest pace with significant congestion in the prominent/midfield band — favours horses with genuine tactical flexibility who can travel kindly in mid-division and produce a sustained finish, slightly rewarding the hold-up runners who are true closers (Bourbon Blues, Loz Vegas, Lean d'Aislingean) and the best prominent types who are genuinely comfortable racing there.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Evanesco Dictates, Prominents Profit
scenarios.trigger: If Evanesco gets a clean break and the field settles into a single-file parade behind him at a fair pace, rewarding those prominent runners who actually secure their position.
scenarios.body: Evanesco controls the tempo on the rail at Goodwood, the congestion behind him resolves into a settled order by halfway, and the race becomes a test of class over the final three furlongs where prominent runners with genuine quality can peel off his back. Harmonics, Gonna Fly, Savvy Disko and Decade Of Time — all confirmed prominent types who should hold their position — are the chief beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Pressure Blows Up Early
scenarios.trigger: If the redistirbuted prominent horses (Lion of Alba, Dark Whisper, Ciarrai Abu) force an early scramble for position and push Evanesco into a faster-than-ideal gallop.
scenarios.body: The first quarter-mile becomes a battle for prominent slots, the pace quickens materially, and the race is run at a clip that stretches stamina reserves over Goodwood's testing finishing hill. This plays directly into the hands of the hold-up horses who are genuine closers, particularly Bourbon Blues who has the form and course experience to reel in tiring front-runners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If Evanesco is unchallenged and deliberately dawdles, creating a truly slow early gallop that compresses the field and sets up a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With the field bunched and no pace to run at, the race degenerates into a sprint from two furlongs out on quick ground, suiting horses with a sharp turn of foot rather than stayers. Decade Of Time and Birgham Dub, both with strong form over shorter trips stepping up, could benefit from this sprint-finish scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tired Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong throughout and prominent horses are found out by the uphill finish, opening the door for true hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: Goodwood's finishing hill exacts a toll on horses that have raced freely, and if the tempo has been honest, horses tracked from off the pace with stamina in reserve can produce a strong late challenge. Bourbon Blues and Loz Vegas, operating from their natural hold-up positions, are best placed if this shape materialises, though neither has top-level form to inspire full confidence.

watchPoints.text: Lion of Alba, Dark Whisper and Ciarrai Abu are all natural pace-pressers who cannot all settle prominently — watch the first furlong for a scramble that could force Evanesco into a faster gallop than anticipated.

Evanesco carries a STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) indicating he has been racing away from front-running recently — if he is slow into stride or fails to stride on, the pace structure of the entire race collapses.

Dark Whisper is unbeaten in three but has never faced a field this large or a trip this long — if Jamie Spencer has to work to find a position, her stamina over 1m2f on this undulating track is an untested quantity.

Harmonics is the highest-rated horse for the in-form Gosden yard (7/19 T14) and represents a well-managed progression from back-to-back wins — watch how Shane Foley positions her in the early stages as a signal of the stable's confidence.

Bourbon Blues has run at Goodwood four times and finished placed over 1m2f here — on a day when the race is run to suit hold-up types, his course knowledge and Joe Leavy's tactical awareness make him a live runner from off the pace.

races.name: Markel Richmond Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Adaay of Scarlett
runners_data.note: Consistent course specialist with five Goodwood runs all on similar going, recording two wins and three places including a string of seconds at this trip — naturally prominent, well-placed with Oisin Murphy, and likely to secure a front-rank position without trouble; the repetitive placed form raises questions about a winning turn.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in fine recent fettle, Adaay of Scarlett has finished second in each of his last three starts after back-to-back wins, showing he retains ability; with experience of today's trip and going and 21 days fresh, he rates the one to beat from stall two.

runners_data.name: Big Cigar
runners_data.note: Won at Goodwood and Stavordale on quick ground and carries strong form claims, but the reality of this field is that he is a natural front-runner who will be crowded out of his preferred position early and is asked to race from further back than ideal, which tempers confidence despite his raw ability.|
runners_data.comment: Big Cigar won last time out and has run over today's trip, but that fifth two starts back is a blot on an otherwise solid recent record; 128 lb from stall seven is the challenge facing him here.

runners_data.name: Cut A Dash
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's filly has a win and a fourth on this course at this trip, both on similar going, giving her strong course credentials; she is a genuine prominent racer, 44 days off and stepping up slightly in class to Group 2, but Sean Levey keeps things simple and she should find her position naturally.|
runners_data.comment: Cut A Dash won two starts back and returns on familiar distance and going terms, with our rating of 105 marking him out as a leading threat from stall 8; the main concern is whether 44 days off has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Flann Sunna
runners_data.note: Two wins from two at Goodwood over six furlongs with William Buick aboard is an outstanding profile, but this horse is a natural prominent type who has been placed further back in the mapping because the field is loaded with pace — Buick's experience should help recover some ground early, and the unbeaten course record demands respect.|
runners_data.comment: Flann Sunna rates below the field on our figures despite back-to-back wins in his last two starts, and that speed rating of 69 gives little encouragement against stronger company here; he has run over today's trip and comes in fresh enough at 20 days, but it is hard to get enthusiastic from stall 10 carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Hickory Lad
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's consistent performer has five runs over this course and trip with wins on quick and soft ground, showing genuine versatility and a willing attitude; like Flann Sunna he is a prominent horse shown at the rear due to redistribution, and from that berth his chance depends on traffic clearance rather than raw ability.|
runners_data.comment: Hickory Lad arrives in fine recent trim — a winner two starts back and third last time out, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour at 128 lb from stall nine; the main risk is whether that weight anchors him late.

runners_data.name: Jaan Ki Tukri
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and likely to lead unchallenged; Clive Cox's juvenile won over this course and trip last time, wears a hood, and Hector Crouch should be able to set a measured pace that plays to her strengths — she is the key pace reference for the whole race.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of ten on our figures and his speed rating lags behind the principals, making him hard to fancy at the weights despite carrying 128 lb from stall five. That recent win offers some hope, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Man's Best Friend
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners the highest-rated horse in the field at OR 120 with a course win last time, and as a natural prominent type he should have the class and jockey quality to slot in directly behind the leader; the eight-day turnaround is short but O'Brien and Moore routinely run back quickly at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Rated lowest in the field and his speed figure of 66 gives little encouragement, though he does bring a win eight days ago and experience of today's trip and conditions — hard to fancy against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Mr Macartney
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and showed a brief moment of form with a win at Goodwood earlier, but has since finished sixth, seventh and seventh in his last three; a natural prominent runner who will struggle to get that position here, and the recent poor form compounds concerns about whether this level is beyond him.|
runners_data.comment: Mr Macartney showed what he's capable of with a win four starts back, but three subsequent finishes of seventh, seventh and sixth suggest he's in a difficult patch; has run over today's trip and going before, and 40 days off could freshen him up.

runners_data.name: Night In Vegas
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly won at Goodwood in good-to-firm earlier this season and returned to finish fifth in a stronger race, giving her course form on both sides of the ledger; 44 days off and a natural prominent type, she should find a berth just off the pace and represents each-way interest at a price.|
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins boost his claims, though he's been off 44 days and drops marginally below the official mark on our rating; has run over today's trip and going, and stall three is his draw from 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Where Love Lives
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's juvenile won twice at five furlongs on similar ground before finishing last of twelve at Goodwood, which raises a distance or race-fitness query; naturally a prominent racer who is likely to be squeezed back from her preferred pitch in this traffic-heavy field, and 40 days off with a trainer who has had no runners in the past 14 days adds to the uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Where Love Lives won two of his last three starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a serious contender from stall one carrying 128 lb — the concern is that unplaced effort on his most recent outing needs excusing.

races.paceDynamic: Jaan Ki Tukri is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should bowl along in front at a sustainable clip on good-to-firm Goodwood turf, dictating her own fractions without being pressured into a suicidal gallop. Behind her, Adaay of Scarlett, Man's Best Friend, Cut A Dash and Night In Vegas all want the prominent berths just off the pace, creating a tight, congested group two to three lengths off the leader that will compress through the dip and risk traffic issues two out. This field holds more prominent-minded types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly — Big Cigar, Where Love Lives and Mr Macartney are natural prominent racers who are most likely to be shuffled back into midfield against their instincts, with Man's Best Friend and Adaay of Scarlett best placed to actually secure their preferred spots given class and jockey quality. The race shape strongly favours a horse that can sit in a comfortable prominent position just behind the front-runner and produce a clean, unimpeded run from two furlongs out — horses with tactical speed and a turn of foot off a controlled pace rather than those relying on a truly fast gallop or a deep hold-up run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jaan Ki Tukri Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Jaan Ki Tukri sets a sustainable pace and the prominent horses immediately behind get a clean passage into the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Jaan Ki Tukri dictates from the front at a comfortable gallop while Man's Best Friend and Adaay of Scarlett travel powerfully in the first two behind, producing their challenge straightening up without traffic interference. This is the dominant shape given the lone front-runner dynamic and the quality of the prominent brigade, rewarding horses with tactical speed and class.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Congestion Causes Interference
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent types collide for position two to three furlongs out, creating a bunched scramble that benefits a horse who finds daylight quickest.
scenarios.body: Traffic becomes a genuine problem through the dip as Adaay of Scarlett, Cut A Dash, Night In Vegas and whoever of Big Cigar/Man's Best Friend gets forward all race in a tight group, producing interference at a critical point. The horse who finds a gap first and travels widest into the straight gains the decisive advantage, suiting those with the highest cruising speed and a willing response.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Jaan Ki Tukri's fractions are genuinely slow enough that she builds a significant lead and the bunched pack behind cannot collectively reel her in.
scenarios.body: With the field bottled up behind and no-one willing to press early, Jaan Ki Tukri steals first run and the prominent horses waste energy navigating each other before delivering their challenge too late. A slow-run sprint like this suits the front-runner most but also offers hope to any horse who can extricate from the pack and sustain a long run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Emerge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and redistributed horses who were unable to get their natural position somehow produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Big Cigar, Where Love Lives or Mr Macartney to find a passage from unnatural hold-up positions and pick off tiring rivals in the final hundred yards, which is a low-probability outcome given none are true hold-up horses and the going favours those with early tactical speed. It cannot be entirely dismissed on a track that can produce late finishers, but the style mismatch heavily suppresses this shape.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion danger: Adaay of Scarlett, Man's Best Friend, Cut A Dash and Night In Vegas all want the same two or three spots directly behind Jaan Ki Tukri — watch for bumping and switching at the two-furlong pole where the course drops into the dip.

Big Cigar and Where Love Lives, both natural front-runners, will be shuffled back against their instincts at the start — watch for either attempting to push forward aggressively in the first furlong and disrupting the formation around them.

Jaan Ki Tukri's pace judgment is critical: if Hector Crouch underestimates the field's cruising speed and crawls through the first three furlongs, the whole pack will overrun her turning for home and compress into a chaotic sprint finish.

Flann Sunna is unbeaten at this course and trip but William Buick will need to extract him from an unnatural rear position — watch whether Buick elects to push forward from the outset or accepts the back-end slot, as it will significantly alter the horse's winning chance.

Man's Best Friend ran just eight days ago — watch the pre-race market move closely; if Ryan Moore and O'Brien are bullish, the short turnaround is a non-issue at this level, but any market drift from a morning price would be a significant signal.

races.name: Maison Perrier Gordon Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Geryon
runners_data.note: Strong Goodwood course form (won over 9f here) is the standout credential; Colin Keane provides a major positional upgrade and the step up to 1m4f looks a natural progression for a horse already placed at 1m2f at this track on similar ground, making him the likeliest prominent challenger to Venetian Lace.
runners_data.comment: Geryon is the one to beat here — a winner last time out, with a second three starts back, he returns on going he has encountered before and has the highest rating in the field. The 132 lb burden is the one thing to watch.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Brilliance
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett has the figures (7/47 over 14 days) and Hector Crouch knows the horse; won at 9f and 10f on soft, but the two runs at 12f came on soft/heavy — the Good to Firm ground here at this longer trip is an open question worth noting, and the 25-day absence after a soft-ground effort at Goodwood last time deserves monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Bay Of Brilliance posted back-to-back wins three and four starts back and returns here fresh enough on 25 days' rest, having run over today's trip before. The main risk is his unplaced effort last time out, which must be answered.

runners_data.name: Enceladus
runners_data.note: Two wins on the spin including a course-and-distance success at Goodwood on good ground give him a compelling angle; however, a natural front-runner pushed into midfield by the weight of prominent types means he will be racing against his instincts, and with 42 days off for Joseph O'Brien's yard (T14: 16/67), the combination of positional compromise and the absence needs pricing in.
runners_data.comment: Enceladus has won his last two starts, but our rating ranks him sixth of seven here, and his speed figure of 86 leaves him needing significant improvement. Third three starts back and fourth starts back add some consistency, though he faces a stiff task on these assessments.

runners_data.name: Magnetude
runners_data.note: Won at 1m2f on good ground at Goodwood which is directly relevant, but the two subsequent runs at 1m6f here were modest (2nd and 8th) and the stable's 14-day figures (16/46) are unspectacular; naturally wants to race forward and will be inconvenienced by being denied that berth in a field stacked with prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of seven on our figures and his speed rating of 83 trails the field, making him hard to fancy despite an eighth two starts back sandwiched between better efforts — though he has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sahara King
runners_data.note: Twice placed at 1m2f on good ground at Goodwood, giving him a genuine course affinity, but the step to 1m4f is unproven and Richard Hannon's 14-day record (9/49) is modest; mapped to the rear against his natural prominent style, so he needs a different race shape to the one that appears likely.
runners_data.comment: Sahara King was unplaced last time out after consecutive second-place finishes two and three starts back, and a winner five starts back, so the form is mixed. Familiarity with today's going helps, but 40 days off and 129 lb make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Shaihaan
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's runner has a win at 1m2f on heavy ground at the Curragh but only one visit to Goodwood (5th, 12f, good) and the trainer has sent out zero winners from 14 runners over the past fortnight; relegated from his natural prominent berth by the volume of pace-minded horses, he faces a stiff task racing out of character.
runners_data.comment: Shaihaan brings solid recent form to the table — third two starts back and a winner four starts back — and he has experience of both today's trip and going conditions; his rating of 109 underlines his claims. The fifth last time out is the one to forgive.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lace
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will dictate every aspect of the tempo — Jason Hart can dictate on this descent and exploit the lack of challengers; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that this is a horse whose winning form has largely come in smaller, less pressured fields, and Good to Firm ground over 1m4f at Goodwood represents a stiffer test than anything on her recent form string.
runners_data.comment: Venetian Lace showed sharp ability when second and third in consecutive starts, and her experience on today's going is a clear asset carrying 126 lb; the risk is that two subsequent below-par efforts — seventh and ninth in her last two — leave her needing to bounce back sharply.

races.paceDynamic: Venetian Lace is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of seven and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to push her along — she will stride out from the gate, control the tempo through Goodwood's early descent, and dictate a sustainable, unhurried gallop that keeps the race well within herself. Behind her, Bay Of Brilliance and Geryon are the next most likely to press into a prominent position, meaning the race settles into a compressed, single-file shape with a modest pace rather than a thorough test of stamina. This configuration historically rewards the horse that can travel smoothly in the slipstream, produce a sustained rather than explosive acceleration, and pick up fluently on Good to Firm ground — a profile that suits prominent stalkers who can close from second or third rather than deep hold-up types who need fractions to be run on their behalf. The field holds more prominent-minded types than the race shape can accommodate in genuine front-rank positions: Shaihaan, Enceladus, and Magnetude are all natural prominent racers who will be shuffled back against their will, meaning their form figures in that role become harder to reproduce here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Venetian Lace Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Venetian Lace is allowed to stride clear and regulate a gentle, uncontested tempo that never truly tests the field's stamina.
scenarios.body: Venetian Lace sets a fair but undemanding pace down the hill and into the straight, conserving enough energy to quicken again when pressed inside the final two furlongs; horses that travel prominently in her wake without burning energy will be best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate gallop compresses the field and a horse sitting second or third produces a clean, sustained run from two out to wear down Venetian Lace.
scenarios.body: Goodwood's undulating finish rewards a horse that has covered the ground economically and still holds a gear approaching the straight; with Venetian Lace not fully pressured early, the first horse to really pick up past her takes the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Stamina Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions are quicker than expected due to jockeys pushing for position and the contest becomes a genuine test of 1m4f stamina on fast ground.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop stretches the field on the run to the home turn and the winner will be the horse with the deepest reserves of stamina; Enceladus, who has won at this trip on good ground at Goodwood, becomes a more credible danger if the race is truly run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Venetian Lace fades tamely in the straight having been over-confident in front, allowing a horse forced to the rear to get a clear run and finish best of all.
scenarios.body: With Sahara King and Shaihaan both pushed further back than their natural positions suggest, this scenario depends on them racing out of role and benefiting from a late collapse of the front rank — a low-probability conjunction of events.

watchPoints.text: Venetian Lace's early sections — if Hart uses the downhill stretch to steal an unusually large lead, no horse in this field has the tactical speed or positional nous to go after her, and the race could be over long before the straight.

Geryon's opening position — Colin Keane must slot in directly behind Venetian Lace rather than getting outpaced to midfield; if Enceladus, Shaihaan, or Magnetude fight for the same early berth, Geryon could get squeezed out of his optimal prominent spot.

Bay Of Brilliance's going suitability — all three wins have come on soft or heavy; Good to Firm at Goodwood over 1m4f is an unproven combination, and if the ground rides quick it may blunt his finishing effort.

Enceladus's positional battle from the gate — he has won at course and distance and will want to be prominent; watch whether Dylan Browne McMonagle attempts to push forward past the redistributed field or accepts midfield, as that decision will determine whether his form figures are replicable here.

Magnetude's draw and early stride — Oisin Murphy will be conscious of his horse's natural front-running preference; any jostling between Magnetude, Shaihaan, and Enceladus for positions that cannot all be filled is a potential incident flashpoint on the early descent at Goodwood.

runners_data.comment: Moments Of Joy showed genuine promise with a second in her last five starts, and has experience over today's trip and conditions — the worry is she's been winless in recent starts and returns after a 46-day absence.

races.paceDynamic: See The Fire is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only five runners on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood, she is highly likely to dictate a controlled, unchallenged gallop from the outset — no rival has the profile or incentive to chase her into a duel. That uncontested lead typically produces a steady early pace that compresses into a stamina-and-class test from the home turn, where the ability to quicken off a modest tempo becomes the decisive factor. Diamond Necklace and Botagoz are both natural prominent racers who cannot all occupy their preferred position behind the leader in such a small field; with See The Fire taking the front, those two are most likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than their redistributed midfield slots suggest, though one or both may be shuffled back slightly. This race shape — a leader who controls fractions, a fast surface, and a compressed field — suits horses who can travel prominently, maintain their rhythm on Good to Firm, and produce a sustained finish; confirmed prominent types and those with a turn of foot over this trip have the clearest edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: See The Fire Controls, Kicks
scenarios.trigger: If See The Fire dictates an uncontested, honest-but-not-suicidal gallop and quickens off the home turn before rivals can close.
scenarios.body: See The Fire, having dominated similar fields over course and distance and carrying strong in-role credentials, uses her position and fitness from a 43-day break to hold on; the small field and lack of a genuine challenger in the early stages means she never has her rhythm disrupted.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If See The Fire's pace is just slow enough that a prominent tracker — Friendly Soul or Diamond Necklace — is travelling supremely well and collars her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With five runners and a compressed field, Friendly Soul or Diamond Necklace can sit a length or two off the leader and time their challenge perfectly, their superior OR and class advantage telling in the final 150 yards on quick ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unbeaten Diamond Necklace Stamps Class
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Necklace's unbeaten five-race sequence, elite trainer and Ryan Moore's tactical intelligence allow her to dominate despite being nudged slightly out of her natural berth.
scenarios.body: Moore is likely to press forward from the outset to reclaim a prominent position regardless of the redistribution dynamic, and Diamond Necklace's five straight wins — including at Goodwood — suggest she has the class to win regardless of shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out, allowing Moments Of Joy to produce a late run from the back.
scenarios.body: Moments Of Joy's recent form reads 25-640 and she has finished in the rear in her last three, making this scenario heavily dependent on a pace collapse that simply looks unlikely given See The Fire's controlled front-running style; even if closers do benefit, there is no genuine hold-up horse here to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: See The Fire sets an uncontested, deceptively fast pace on Good to Firm — watch whether Oisin Murphy increases the tempo turning in, because if he does the race becomes a sprint finish that could strand any horse not travelling smoothly at that point.

Diamond Necklace will likely push forward aggressively under Ryan Moore to reclaim her natural prominent position — if she travels into contention within two lengths of See The Fire, she becomes the most dangerous horse in the race entering the straight.

Friendly Soul is 43 days off the track; Gosden horses often return fresh and ready, but watch the pre-race market move — if she drifts, the layoff may be a concern; if she shortens, Buick's hold of the situation tracking the pace is a major advantage.

Botagoz is the youngest and least experienced runner in the field (only four career starts), and a small, fast Group 1 on Good to Firm may come too soon — watch for her to be outpaced once the tempo increases in the final quarter mile.

With only five runners, gaps are likely to be minimal and the race may be decided by a matter of a length or two; watch for bunching on the home turn and the premium placed on a horse who can quicken sharply from a prominent position rather than grind it out.

races.paceDynamic: Schrodinger's Cat is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner sprint and is expected to bowl along from the gates at a sustainable, uncontested tempo on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood's straight five. With no genuine rival prepared to fight for the lead, the pace will be controlled rather than frantic, producing a clean gallop that rewards horses travelling economically in the first two furlongs and finding a stride into the rising Goodwood finish. The field contains significantly more pace than can be accommodated up front — River Spey, Quantum Power, One And Gone, Noble Vow, and U S S Charleston are all natural prominent racers who are likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield against their instincts, with Naana's Shadow and Manatee Mehmas best positioned to actually secure prominent berths behind the leader. This scenario — a single front-runner setting an honest but manageable gallop — most strongly favours genuine prominent-to-midfield runners who can travel close to the pace and quicken on the rising ground, rather than true hold-up horses relying on a collapse at the front that is unlikely to materialise.

scenarios.label: A

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late

watchPoints.text: Naana's Shadow's three Goodwood 5f wins under Murphy make her the most track-specific threat in the field — watch how quickly she settles in behind Schrodinger's Cat at the break.

Quantum Power has won three times at Goodwood and the visor goes on, but his ability to secure a prominent pitch ahead of River Spey and One And Gone will decide whether his course record can be exploited — watch the first furlong scrimmage closely.

Truly Glamorous wore a hood and posted consecutive Goodwood wins — if she is able to get a clear run from the rear she can finish with real purpose, but in an 18-runner field traffic could easily block her late challenge.

Old Is Gold returns from 97 days off for Balding and Doyle — if the yard has him spot-on after that break he is capable on course form, but a fitness question mark hangs over the run and he should be monitored in the market for late support.

With 18 runners over a straight 5f and a congested pace map, draw position and a clean break from the stalls could be decisive — horses that miss the kick in this shape have almost no opportunity to recover on a flat, short-course sprint.

runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with an eighth last time out doing little to inspire confidence, Primal ranks 16th of 18 on our figures; the trainer's strong recent strike rate and experience over today's trip and going are the slender positives.

runners_data.name: Rbflying
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse from Tim Easterby's yard that has been redistributed to midfield on the map; four runs at Goodwood on similar going without a win and limited upside in form figures — the redistribution reflects the deep field more than any upgrading of Rbflying's prospects.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 17th of 18 on our figures, Rbflying faces a stiff task here; a third two starts back offers a crumb of hope, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but the handicap weight of 121 lb from stall 10 adds to his burden.

races.paceDynamic: Cilician is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse willing to lead from the front in an 18-runner field, will stride into a clear early advantage down Goodwood's opening straight without any meaningful challenge for the lead. Behind him, a cluster of prominent-types — Shadow King, Sword Salute, My A'Ali Baba, Caeruleus, Everatease and Mia Fantasia — will jostle keenly for the favoured positions just off the pace, creating a competitive but not punishing early tempo on Good To Firm ground. The field holds more genuine front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; Cilician will lead unchallenged, while Shadow King, Sword Salute and Mia Fantasia are best-placed to actually claim the prominent slots given course form and jockey quality, with Cash Cove, Wise And Wonderful and Crazy Cubana likely shuffled wider and further back than they would ideally want. One controlled, single front-runner dictating at a fair pace on fast ground over 7f at Goodwood — a track that rewards those racing handy and making smooth progress into the straight — strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can travel into the race and kick, rather than those held up deep who must produce a sustained late run through a tightly packed field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cilician Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Cilician leads alone at a sustainable gallop and prominent chasers pick him off in the final furlong without a dramatic pace collapse.
scenarios.body: Cilician sets a measured tempo in front, keeping the field honest but not suicidal, allowing the prominent horses tucked just behind to race into contention rounding the home turn; on Good To Firm ground over 7f this is the textbook Goodwood shape where those covering the leader smoothly into the straight hold a decisive positional edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of prominent types press Cilician harder than expected mid-race, setting a hot gallop that burns them off and opens the door for hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: Increased pressure on Cilician causes the pace to quicken significantly through the middle section, stretching the field and tiring those that raced keenly in the prominent group; genuine hold-up horses who settle and travel sweetly through the field find energy reserves the prominent runners have spent.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble, Surprise Value
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent group leads to early jostling, interference and uneven splits that create a messy, no-one-controls shape.
scenarios.body: Several prominent types forced wider or off their stride in the early stages produce a fractured pace, rewarding those who find a clean passage and quicken off a steady-then-sharp tempo; horses with strong Goodwood course form and tactical jockeys navigate this best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Cilician is allowed a completely unchallenged lead at a dawdle and simply sprints clear from the front entering the final 2f.
scenarios.body: With zero pressure, Cilician builds a winning lead by halfway and the prominent chasers, having had the race run to suit a hold-up closer, cannot reel in a fresh front-runner who has barely been asked a question; this scenario requires the prominent group to inexplicably forget to apply pressure, making it a low-probability outlier.

watchPoints.text: Mia Fantasia and Wise And Wonderful both won over course and distance recently — whichever of the two secures the cleaner prominent position heading into the straight is likely to pose the most serious threat to Cilician.

The congested prominent group (Shadow King, Sword Salute, My A'Ali Baba, Caeruleus, Everatease) risks early crowding and checking in an 18-runner field on a track where early position is hard to recover — watch for interference in the first two furlongs.

Cilician's STYLE_FIT flag is worth monitoring in running: if another horse challenges him for the lead before halfway and forces him to race genuinely hard, his chance of lasting home drops sharply and the shape switches entirely.

Cash Cove, Wise And Wonderful and Crazy Cubana are all genuine prominent types racing out of their natural position — if any of them manages to push forward early against expectations, the pace map changes and the tempo could quicken materially.

Agitator's fading-finish flag combined with the step to 7f makes it a horse to watch as a market mover rather than a race factor — if heavily backed it may signal stable confidence overriding the form concern, but the profile does not suit this shape.

runners_data.name: Intense Vision
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who rarely features early; trainer Oli Rix has a modest 14-day strike rate and the 42-day absence is a minor flag, though Goodwood form exists — likely needs something to go wrong up front to get competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Showed a smart vein of form with back-to-back wins three and four starts back, but he disappointed last time out and the 42-day break adds a fitness query; has run over today's trip and carries 135 lb from stall 16.

runners_data.name: Exclusive Code
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner; James Doyle gives her every chance to dictate from the front, Goodwood mile winning form is a major asset, and racing unchallenged for the lead is the single biggest tactical advantage in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Exclusive Code won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating putting him right in contention from stall one; the worry is that unplaced return last time out, now 42 days ago.

runners_data.name: Vincenzo Peruggia
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston-trained hold-up type with a Goodwood winning mark over this trip; the 42-day break is a consideration but the mile on Good to Firm at this track is squarely in his wheelhouse.|
runners_data.comment: Ran unplaced last time but boasts a second three starts back and a win five starts back, giving him something to build on; experience over today's trip and going helps, though 42 days off and a tough 134 lb ask make this a stern test.

runners_data.name: Wild Thoughts
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with six wins in her last seven and headgear noted; Saffie Osborne has been riding her well, she acts on Good to Firm and is one of the likeliest to secure a genuine handy position in the early stages.|
runners_data.comment: Wild Thoughts won four of his last six starts but has drifted to seventh last time out, casting doubt on current form; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 134 lb is a significant burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Richie's Rocket
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's prominent type has been running into placings without winning of late; Hector Crouch takes over and the drop to a mile on quick ground is worth monitoring, but form has been patchy at Goodwood this season.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Richie's Rocket nonetheless catches the eye on our rating of 102, and having run over today's trip and going before, he arrives fit on 26 days' rest — the one to side with here.

runners_data.name: Law Court
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner who has been remarkably consistent in placing at Goodwood over a mile — five runs this season with multiple placed efforts here; Faleh Bughanaim's familiarity with the horse could prove key in a big field.|
runners_data.comment: Law Court has been consistently in the thick of things, finishing second last time out and a winner two starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main query is whether 47 days off the track has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Zennor Storm
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner with headgear noted; recent Goodwood form has disappointed despite winning at Sandown earlier in the season, and his last three runs at this track show no wins — Tom Marquand will need to improve matters.|
runners_data.comment: Zennor Storm showed his best form with back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and going; our rating of 96 suggests he retains ability, but a fourth last time out and a 132 lb burden from stall 13 are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Runswick
runners_data.note: Won last time out and has solid Goodwood experience; Daniel Tudhope is a strong booking and the prominent style means he should be able to position ahead of the redistributed pack, making him one of the more natural prominent types in the race.|
runners_data.comment: Runswick won last time out and was third three starts back, showing consistent recent form, but he faces a stiff ask from stall 19 carrying 132 lb off an official mark of 87 — experience over today's trip and going at least counts in his favour.

runners_data.name: Electric Dreams
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's runner won her last start at Goodwood over this trip; Oisin Murphy is a significant jockey upgrade and only three career runs means there is unexplored upside — the low mileage is a positive at this stage of the season.|
runners_data.comment: Electric Dreams won last time out but that victory came 47 days ago, he ranks a lowly 17th of 20 on our figures, and a speed rating of 70 makes him hard to fancy despite having experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Euston Hall
runners_data.note: Won twice at Goodwood and has course form at this trip; Colin Keane is an excellent jockey in big-field handicaps and Ed Walker's yard is in strong form over 14 days — one of the best-placed prominent types to hold position naturally.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten into sixth last time out after back-to-back wins earlier in his recent form, Euston Hall returns after 41 days and faces a stiff task ranked 15th of 20 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going, and the trainer's 28% strike rate offers some hope.

runners_data.name: Go Rimbaud
runners_data.note: William Buick and John & Thady Gosden combine with a horse whose natural instinct is to race up with the pace; with so many prominent types in the field, he is likely to be shuffled back from his preferred position, which tempers his chance.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip, but Go Rimbaud's fifth two starts back tempers enthusiasm slightly; drawn in stall 15 carrying 130 lb, he has ability on his day yet consistency remains the question at this level.

runners_data.name: Storming Point
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore ride who wants to be close to the pace but, in a field this competitive, will find that ground contested; a genuine prominent racer in profile but the redistribution means Moore may have to settle for a midfield berth against his wishes.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts despite a string of placed efforts, Storming Point has run over today's trip and returns after 30 days, but carrying 130 lb from stall 20 with our rating six pounds below his official mark makes him hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Abundant
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's runner wants to race handy and has placed figures here at Goodwood; similarly, the overcrowded prominent contingent means Sean Levey faces an early tactical battle just to get the position the horse needs to be effective.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent without quite winning, Abundant has been third twice in his last two starts and a winner four starts back, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; the 125 lb burden and draw 17 are the obvious counterweights to a timely 20-day break.

runners_data.name: Kalokalo
runners_data.note: Charles Hills horse with strong staying form at Goodwood over longer trips — this mile trip may be on the sharp side; Jason Watson will try to secure a forward berth but, with his natural style competed for by many rivals, he is likely to be outpaced early.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 16 of 20 on our figures, Kalokalo faces a stiff ask at the bottom of the assessments, and a speed rating of 69 does little to inspire confidence — yet he does arrive in decent nick, third last time out after winning two starts back, with distance and going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: Loblolly
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from Stuart Woods' yard with a sequence of placed efforts but no wins recently; David Egan knows the type and will be patient, but a steady pace here — as projected — makes late delivery from the rear structurally difficult.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Loblolly does bring experience over today's trip and going, and consecutive thirds suggest a degree of consistency — but his ranking of 14th in the field and a speed rating of 75 leave him with plenty to find against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Get Outta Here
runners_data.note: David Menuisier runner who has won at Goodwood over this trip and whose natural tendency is to race prominently; Jamie Spencer is a patient jockey who may elect to settle him back, which could either suit or frustrate.|
runners_data.comment: Get Outta Here arrives in fair nick — placed last time out and a winner three starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, though our rating of 88 suggests he may face stiffer competition than his official mark of 79 implies.

runners_data.name: Aqua Bear
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner whose best work has been at shorter trips at Goodwood; Billy Loughnane will likely find the horse racing further back than ideal given the prominent-type congestion, and seven-furlong form hints this mile on fast ground may stretch him.|
runners_data.comment: Aqua Bear has experience of today's trip and conditions, and his third two starts back shows he can get into the mix, but unplaced runs either side of that effort are a concern; 124 lb from stall 18 adds to the task.

runners_data.name: Dumuji
runners_data.note: Clive Cox runner returning from 80 days off — the longest absence in the field — with only three career starts; P J McDonald takes the ride but the absence and inexperience in a 20-runner handicap are significant unknowns.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten in his last two starts and returning after 80 days off, Dumuji is a difficult proposition ranked 18th of 20 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, and his win three starts back offers the one crumb of hope.

runners_data.name: Storm Point
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's second string alongside Euston Hall; Kieran Shoemark picks him up and he has won over this trip, but recent Goodwood form has been poor and the redistribution confirms he will struggle to reproduce his natural prominent position in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Storm Point has looked inconsistent in recent starts — seventh last time out and sixth three starts back undermine two wins in his last five — and he ranks last on our figures, with a speed rating of 65 doing him no favours. A firing trainer and experience over today's trip offer slim reasons for hope.

runners_data.name: Mr Seagull
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer runner with headgear noted who has been beaten out of sight in recent starts; David Probert's experience in big-field handicaps helps, but the OR of 77 — lowest in the field — and a poor recent run sequence make this a tough ask.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Mr Seagull has at least been running consistently around the midfield placings, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 122 lb from stall 12, his rating of 92 suggests he holds claims, though his recent record offers little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Exclusive Code is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 20-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure — she can roll along at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood's mile without being challenged for the lead. The absence of a second front-runner means the pace is unlikely to be truly fierce, which compresses the field and makes a strong case for horses who can race prominently behind her and use that prime position into the Goodwood straight. A large bloc of natural prominent types — including Go Rimbaud, Storming Point, Wild Thoughts, Law Court, Euston Hall and Kalokalo — will all contest the same ground behind Exclusive Code, meaning several will be shuffled wider or further back than they would choose, reducing the tactical value of their preferred style. This race shape — moderate tempo, single leader, crowded mid-pack — strongly favours genuine prominent racers who can secure a front-rank berth early and sustain it, particularly those with proven Goodwood form; true hold-up horses face an attritional task in a large field where the pace is not hot enough to string things out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Exclusive Code dictates a measured gallop and prominent types behind her secure the best ground into the straight.
scenarios.body: Exclusive Code sets a sustainable tempo, the race stays together until the final two furlongs, and horses who secured a handy position behind her get first run on the field; the lack of genuine pace pressure means closers from the rear struggle to generate momentum to pick off those already travelling well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late, Class Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is so sedate that the race becomes a sprint finish in the final furlong and higher-class horses dominate.
scenarios.body: With Exclusive Code unchallenged and slowing proceedings, the race degenerates into a late dash; horses with the best raw speed and highest OR ratings who can quicken off a slow pace are most advantaged.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Creates Opening
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion of multiple prominent types scrambling for position behind Exclusive Code creates an uneven early pace that benefits hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Several natural front-runners forced back — Storming Point, Go Rimbaud, Kalokalo — create brief surges of pace as they jockey for position, which strings the race out enough to suit horses delivered late with a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Exclusive Code is allowed to bowl along completely unchallenged and the field is caught flat-footed turning for home.
scenarios.body: With zero pace pressure James Doyle can control every fraction, conserve Exclusive Code for a sustained run into the straight, and the field — disorganised from early positional battles — fails to coordinate a challenge in time.

watchPoints.text: Wild Thoughts and Euston Hall are both natural prominent types in a field where prominent runners are at a premium — watch whether both can secure a front-rank berth at the start, as whoever wins that battle early has a structural edge for the rest of the race.|

Exclusive Code (James Doyle) may attempt to coast in front from the off — if she is allowed more than three lengths of daylight heading into the home straight, horses held up at the rear will have too much ground to make up on Good to Firm.|

Go Rimbaud and Storming Point are both tagged as redistributed prominent types with high-profile jockeys in Buick and Moore; if either manages to force their way to the front rank against expectation, the pace dynamic changes and the scenario probabilities shift materially.|

Electric Dreams is the least-exposed horse in the race with only three starts — her Goodwood-mile win last time and the Oisin Murphy booking mean she is worth monitoring in-running to see whether she can slot into a handy position from a wide draw.|

The 80-day break for Dumuji (Clive Cox/P J McDonald) is the most extreme absence in the field — watch market moves before the off as a market move would imply connections are happy, while a drifter should be dismissed entirely in a competitive 20-runner handicap.|
